stories.title: US strikes Iran as state media reports four killed at wedding party
stories.summary: American forces resumed strikes against Iran on Tuesday, US Central Command has said in a statement. The Iranian Red Crescent said four people including a young child were killed, and more than 50 injured, when shrapnel from a US missile attack hit a home where a wedding celebration was taking place in Sirik in southern Iran. Centcom said the strikes followed "recent attempted attacks" by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) against commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and "American service members deployed to the region". The IRGC said the US would regret the strikes, and Iranian news agencies reported that retaliatory missile and drone attacks on US targets had begun. Donald Trump, when the US strikes were announced on Tuesday afternoon, warned that Iran would be hit again at "a much harder and higher level" if it retaliated. The attack follows the first known US strikes on Iran since late July earlier this week, when forces attacked two rocket launchers on Larak Island in the Strait. Tehran retaliated by firing missiles at air bases in Jordan and a drone at the UAE. Centcom said US forces had begun striking IRGC targets at 12:00 ET (16:00 GMT). As well as the Sirik attack, other reports said projectiles had hit the areas of Chabahar and Konarak and an airport in Jiroft, and that explosions were heard in Qeshm island and Bandar Abbas. The IRGC was reported as saying it had launched a barrage of ballistic missiles at a US Marine base in Jordan's Aqaba in retaliation for the Sirik attack. Jordan's state-affiliated Al-Mamlaka network reported that the country's national security centre had warned residents of the Aqaba and Mafraq governates of falling debris, adding that the warning had since ended. Trump said Tuesday's "large and powerful" strikes were a response to Iran's targeting of a US military base in Jordan, adding the country had "failed" at adding sea mines to the Strait.

stories.title: Global bond selloff deepens as US launches fresh attacks on Iran
stories.summary: Oil prices rose, stocks fell and bond yields spiked after the US launched fresh attacks on Iranian targets. Japan's 10-year bond yield hit 3% for the first time since 1996. The deepening global selloff comes amid fears over rising inflation and concern over mounting government debt - which in the US has risen above 40 trillion dollars. Meanwhile, in the single-currency Eurozone, inflation rose to the highest level in three years in August, driven by higher energy prices.

stories.title: Special services always in contact — Putin on CIA director's Russia visit
stories.summary: BISHKEK, September 2. Contacts between special services are always maintained, including direct contacts between their heads, Russian President Vladimir Putin commented on the recent visit to Russia of US CIA Director John Ratcliffe. "Contacts between special services are always maintained. Direct contacts are also maintained between the heads of special services," the head of state said, answering questions from reporters. Ratcliffe arrived in Russia on August 25. Russian Foreign Intelligence Service Director Sergey Naryshkin confirmed that he had met with the CIA chief. He also said that they had discussed issues within the scope of intelligence services.

stories.title: Football: Europe's top clubs scramble for last-minute signings
stories.summary: The football transfer window is entering its final hours. After a lot of last-minute negotiations, Manchester City are reported to have reached an agreement with Chelsea to sign Argentinian midfielder Enzo Fernandez for 125 million pounds – the biggest fee in a 3.3 billion euro spending frenzy by the top clubs. Meanwhile Aston Villa have signed 18-year-old winger Ibrahim Mbaye from PSG for 55 million euros.
